desc:
A single-threaded program has n functions numbered 0 to n - 1. Functions call each other (a function may even call itself), and a log records every call. Each log entry is [id, type, t]:

  • type = 0: a call of function id starts at the very beginning of time unit t.
  • type = 1: the call of function id that is currently open and innermost ends at the very end of time unit t, so unit t still belongs to it.

Only one function runs at any moment: the most recently started call that has not ended. When a call starts, the call that invoked it pauses until it ends. Time units in which no call is open belong to nobody.

Return an array res of length n where res[f] is the exclusive time of function f: the number of time units in which a call of f was the running one, summed over all its calls.

Example: n = 2, logs = [[0,0,0],[1,0,2],[1,1,5],[0,1,6]]. Function 0 runs in units 0, 1 and 6 (3 units); function 1 runs in units 2 to 5 (4 units). The answer is [3, 4].
constraints: 0 ≤ id < n, type is 0 or 1, 0 ≤ t ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>

The logs are valid: calls are properly nested, every call ends, and events appear in time order (a start has t at least the previous event's t, and strictly greater if the previous event was an end; an end has t at least the previous event's t)
hints: Between two consecutive log events, exactly one function (or nobody) is running. Can you charge each gap to the right function?
Keep a stack of open calls. The running function is the top of the stack, and you can remember the time unit at which the current running stretch began.
On a start at t: add t - prev to the function on top (if any), push, set prev = t. On an end at t: add t + 1 - prev to the top, pop, set prev = t + 1.
editorial: Treat a start at time t as the point in time t and an end at time t as the point t + 1, since the end time unit is included. Then the logs describe a sequence of points on a time line, and between two consecutive points the running function is the top of the call stack.

Keep prev, the point where the current stretch began. When a call starts, the caller (stack top) was running from prev until t, so credit it with t - prev, push the new call, and set prev = t. When a call ends at t, the top ran from prev to t + 1: credit t + 1 - prev, pop, and set prev = t + 1. Recursion needs no special handling because credit goes to the id of the stack top. One pass, O(m) time for m logs and O(m) space for the stack, independent of the size of the times.
